## Background and Career Overview {#chap-resume-career}

### Doctorate degree and post-doctorate {#chap-resume-career-PhD}

I have defended [my PhD](/publications/thesis/folio2007thesis.qmd) in Robotics in 2007 within the Robotics, Action, and
Perception (<abbr lang="en" title="Robotics, Action, and Perception">RAP</abbr>)
group of the Laboratory for Analysis and Architecture of Systems[^laas] 
(<abbr lang="en" title="Laboratory for Analysis and Architecture of Systems">LAAS</abbr>), 
<abbr lang="fr" title="Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique">CNRS</abbr>[^cnrs], 
under the supervision of Viviane Cadenat,
Associate Professor at the Paul Sabatier University of Toulouse, France.
Specifically, my PhD thesis was entitled 
["*Multi-sensor-based control strategies and visual signal loss management for mobile robots navigation*"](/publications/thesis/folio2007thesis.qmd#sec-details) [@folio2007thesis].
My thesis subject was to design multi-sensor-based control strategies allowing a mobile
robot to perform vision-based tasks amidst possibly occluding obstacles. Indeed,
the improvement of sensors gave rise to the sensor-based control which allows
defining the robotic task in the sensor space rather than in the configuration
space. 
\
In addition, during my doctorate degree, I also had the opportunity to perform
teaching activities, first as temporary teacher (3 years), and then as teaching
assistant, specifically in French as ["Attaché Temporaire d'Enseignement et de Recherche"]{.french lang="fr"}
(<abbr lang="fr" title="Attaché Temporaire d'Enseignement de Recherche">ATER</abbr>, 1 year),
both for the Paul Sabatier University of Toulouse. These global teaching
experiences have led to a total volume of 308 hETD[^hETD].


Between 2007 and 2008, I joined the Lagadic team at Inria[^Inria]
Rennes-Bretagne Atlantique as a post-doctoral fellow on sensory control
for unmanned aerial vehicles. My postdoctoral fellow has been supported
by _Sensory Control for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles_
(<abbr lang="en" title="Sensory Control for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles">SCUAV</abbr>)
<abbr lang='fr' title='Agence Nationale de la Recherche'>ANR</abbr>
project[^ANR]. The main objective was to improve multi-sensor-based
servoing tasks for unmanned aerial vehicles. The idea was to design
robust control law that combine different sensory data directly at the
control level. Especially, I have contributed to the design of a new
online sensor self-calibration based on the sensor/robot interaction links [@kermorgant2010icra].


### Tenured as associate professor {#resume-career-tenure}

[^laas]: LAAS is a laboratory depending on the CNRS, <http://www.laas.fr>

[^cnrs]: CNRS is the French National Center for Scientific Research, <http://www.cnrs.fr>

[^hETD]: Equivalent TD hours that is in French  [heures équivalentes TD]{.french lang="fr" custom-style="French"}
         (hETD), are the reference hours to calculate the teaching duties. 

<!-- (see also the [index of terms and notations](#glossary))-->

[^Inria]: From French: [Institut national de recherche en informatique et en automatique]{.french lang="fr" custom-style="French"}. \linebreak    <https://www.inria.fr/centre/rennes>

[^ANR]: From French ["Agence Nationale de la Recherche"]{.french lang="fr" custom-style="French"} ([ANR](#glos-ANR)), which is the French National Research Agency, <http://www.agence-nationale-recherche.fr>

[^CNU]: From French ["Conseil National des Université"]{.french lang="fr" custom-style="French"} ([CNU](#glos-CNU)), comprises 57 sections covering different scientific disciplines. The 61^st^ section involves IT engineering, automation and signal processing. \linebreak <https://www.conseil-national-des-universites.fr>

In 2008, I was recruited as Associate Professor for the 61^st^ 
<abbr lang="fr" title='Conseil National des Universités'>CNU</abbr> section[^CNU] at the
Graduate Engineering School
(<abbr lang="fr" title="École Nationale Supérieur d'Ingénieurs">ENSI</abbr>)
of Bourges, which is since 2014 the {{< var INSA-CVL >}}.
Since my tenure, I have been regularly involved in the life of the Institute. I contribute at a local
level to the scientific animations (e.g. organization of laboratory visits),
transfer and training-research relationship. For instance, I regularly attend the
international relations division by accompanying the different
delegations of schools and universities partners during their visits. In March
2017, the direction of the {{< var INSA-CVL >}} given to me the mission of referent _racism and antisemitism_.

As a [lecturer](//teaching/teaching.qmd), I am involved, among others, in the development of
electronics and electrical sciences teaching activities within the Institute. 
Since tenured as associate professor, my average teaching load is about 270 hETD per year.
<!-- Figure \@ref(fig:chapI-teach-load) presents the evolution  of my teaching duty since 2008. -->
Similarly, various responsibilities entrusted to me have also influenced my teaching duties.
Since September 2014, I am in
charge of the option entitled [_Nuclear Energy_](/teaching/SFEN.qmd) of the 5^th^ year (engineer's
degree, M2) of the Industrial Risk Control 
(<abbr lang="fr" title="Maîtrise des Risques Industriels">MRI</abbr>) department. 
Between  2017 and 2020, I have been elected as member of the council department of the Energy, Risks and
Environment (<abbr lang="en" title="Energy, Risks and Environment">ERE</abbr>);
and since November 2020 I am an elected member of the council department of Industrial Risk Control
(<abbr lang="fr" title="Maîtrise des Risques Industriels">MRI</abbr>).


Furthermore, I carry out my research activities with the {{< var PRISME-Laboratory >}}[^PRISME]
in the Robotics team belonging to the Images, Robotics, Automatic control and Signal 
(<abbr lang="fr" title="Images, Robotics, Automatic control and Signal">IRAuS</abbr>) department. 
Since I have been an associate professor, my
field of scientific research mainly focused on the 
_modeling and control for [nano and micro-robots](/research/microrobotics/microrobotics.qmd) in a [biomedical](/research/microrobotics/biomedical.qmd) context_. 
Globally, my main contributions focus on the study of **magnetic medical microrobots** for targeted therapies.
\
Meanwhile, I have also contributed to the development of
micromanipulation activities of the laboratory [@kim2011icra; @kim2012tase].

Finally, on December 3, 2021, I defended [my habilitation](/publications/thesis/folio2021hdr.qmd) (namely in French "[Habilitation à Diriger la Recherche]{lang="fr" .fr}" -- HDR) which I entitled 
["_Magnetic Microrobotics for Biomedical Applications_"](/publications/thesis/folio2021hdr.qmd#sec-details) [@folio2021hdr].



[^PRISME]: PRISME laboratory is from University of Orléans and from INSA [Centre Val de
    Loire]{.fr lang="fr"} (EA 4229). <http://www.univ-orleans.fr/PRISME>
